Idle motion is identity — a still pet reads as broken hardware, so it blinks and breathes continuously.

There is a third movement, and only one face has it. The sick face’s eyes are spirals and they turn; the rotation is what reads as dizzy, so a spiral that had stopped would be the shape shipped with its meaning removed. The generator refuses one without a spinMs, and refuses a spinMs on anything that is not a spiral.

The rhythm is PER STATE, and per set. There is no single blink number. This card used to say 5400 ms was “the firmware's own number, so the two surfaces agree”, and that was true when there was one number. Motion now lives in each face set's JSON beside the geometry, is resolved once by the generator and emitted to all four renderers, so the device, the app, the notification and the prototype still cannot keep separate clocks — there are just more clocks to keep together. Making it per state was the cheapest expressiveness available: it costs no objects and no pixels, because it only changes numbers an animation already uses.

Absence is a state too. The dead face has "motion": null and does not move at all — the missing blink and the missing breathe are the whole message, and a still shape on its own is just a shape. Asleep is the weaker statement: alive and breathing, eyes held shut.

Typing is 1200 ms, staggered 150 ms. Nothing else animates. The transcript deliberately does not: a message bubble cannot tell “I am new” from “I was scrolled back into view”, and only its container knows. Entry animation belongs to the container.

Every set carries its own; resting blink elsewhere is Bloom 5400 ms, Little Computer 4200 ms, Pixel 5400 ms. Sick breathes faster AND shallower than happy, and the generator refuses a set where it does not — shallow and fast is what reads as ill before you have looked at the mouth.
